title: Paul Graham: Why you should go to Silicon Valley, then come back
summary: At YC Startup School Stockholm, Graham argues ambitious founders should move to the center of their field, at least for a while. The big center gives better peers, serendipity, faster decisions, a calibrated sense of your own ability, and a culture of helping. Going and returning also strengthens your home hub.

principles.text: Go to the center of your field; you can return later, but you should at least go.
principles.quote: You can go there for a bit and then come back, but you should at least go.

principles.text: The main benefit of the big center is the best peers: more people and better people, concentrated in one place.
principles.quote: You get the best peers. And in fact, the talent pool expands in two dimensions. The people are better and there's also a lot more of them.

principles.text: Serendipitous meetings with people working on the same ambitious thing are enormously valuable, and big centers produce more of them.
principles.quote: if you're working on something ambitious, there's nothing in the world that's better than serendipitous meetings with people who are working on the same stuff.

principles.text: Silicon Valley investors decide fast because of competition, and it doesn't hurt their returns.
principles.quote: Silicon Valley investors get better returns than European investors despite having to decide so quickly.

principles.text: The biggest advantage of the center is what it does to you: seeing top founders up close makes ambition feel hard but achievable.
principles.quote: for an ambitious person, there is nothing better than a high but definite threshold.

principles.text: Silicon Valley's pay-it-forward culture: help people without keeping score, which lets favors scale.
principles.quote: You just like do favors left and right and don't even keep track of whether you're ahead or behind.
